item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Sat Oct 17, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Downtown Candy Crawl in Ephrata, PA — Sat Oct 17, 12:00 PM — Downtown Ephrata
item.description: After a great turnout in 2025, the Candy Crawl is BACK and scheduled for Saturday, October 17, 2026, from noon to 3pm on Main Street in Ephrata. Mainspring of Ephrata is again co-hosting this family-favorite kids’ event. The Downtown Ephrata Candy Crawl is a free, family-friendly Halloween event held annually in downtown Ephrata, where kids and parents trick-or-treat their way through participating businesses along Main Street and State Street. Beyond candy, the event features activities like a coloring contest, photo booths, pumpkin decorating, a balloon artist, a craft area, and mini games with prizes, drawing over 300 attendees in its first year. Hosted by the Downtown Ephrata Property and Business Owners Association in partnership with Mainspring of Ephrata, the Candy Crawl brings the community together while giving local businesses and organizations a chance to connect with families in a fun, festive setting. item.title: Mercy Seminar, Term 3 — Thu Oct 22, 7:00 PM — Zoom Video Conferencing
item.description: With Father David Peck and Professor Randall Zachman Entirely on Zoom Now in its seventh year, the 2026 Mercy Seminar invites you to explore the profound insights that different faith traditions offer about embracing life and navigating death with grace. How can the certainty of death inspire us to cultivate a deeper focus and a heart full of gratitude, transforming potential feelings of anxiety into a courageous appreciation for the present moment? Is death merely “nothing at all,” or does it open the gateway to an eternal adventure beyond this life? Join us as we delve into selected sacred readings from Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish, Christian, and Muslim scriptures, along with enlightening contemporary secular spiritual writings. Together, we will uncover the wisdom that encourages us to live our best lives and face death not with fear, but with hope and understanding. item.title: Stargazing at Millport — Thu Oct 29, 7:00 PM — Millport Conservancy
item.description: [vc_row][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”540170″] A Spooktacular Night Under the Stars! Celebrate the spooky season with an evening of celestial wonders! Join North Museum at Millport Conservancy on Thursday, October 29, from 7:00–9:00 PM for a FREE night of stargazing! Explore the night sky as we turn our telescopes toward dazzling stars, the magnificent rings of Saturn, and even Algol, the mysterious “Demon Star,” as it begins to dim during its celestial eclipse. If we’re lucky, we might even catch a shooting star or two from the tail end of the Orionid meteor shower! Costumes are encouraged, so dress up, bring a lawn chair, and settle in for a hauntingly good night of astronomy and discovery! When: Thursday, October 29 | 7:00–9:00 PM Where: Millport Conservancy Admission: FREE and open to the public! This event is weather permitting. item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster
